title: Substring Index
statement:
Find where a pattern first appears inside a larger string.

Contract
- `text` and `pattern` may be null. Return `-1` if either argument is null.
- Return the zero-based index of the first occurrence of `pattern` in `text`, or `-1` when it is absent.
- The empty pattern is found at index `0`, including in an empty text.
- Do not use `String.indexOf`, `String.contains`, or regular expressions in the implementation. Do not mutate either input.

Examples
- `substringIndex("abc123", "abc")` returns `0`.
- `substringIndex("abc123", "c12")` returns `2`.
- `substringIndex("abc123", "xyz")` returns `-1`.
hints: A direct nested scan is a useful baseline: try every starting position and compare the pattern characters.
When a partial match fails, keep information about the longest pattern prefix that is also a suffix of what already matched.
Build a KMP prefix table for the pattern, then scan the text once. Intended complexity: O(n) time for the combined input length and O(n) extra space for the pattern table.
inputSyntax: Input: text, then pattern separated by |, for example: abc123|c12
